The signed server parameter offer must select source_clock rtcp-sr-sdes/1 before the peer accepts or emits reports. Unsupported profiles refuse; profile changes cannot alter an installed route. Unclocked media remains explicitly unsynchronized in route diagnostics.

Count actual successful RTP writer submissions and payload octets. Send a bounded SR/SDES compound at most once per second during current media writes, within their original 200ms submission bound. Packetization, rejected queues, report writes and idle timers cannot count as RTP or manufacture readiness.

Bind reports to current receive handles and SSRCs with one common CNAME/NTP reference. Preserve cross-rate offsets despite later per-track arrival variation; zero, old, conflicting, missing or expired reports do not fabricate synchronization. Retired handles reject reports.

Decoded timestamps use the shared receive timeline when mapped. Original Opus timestamp preservation remains in place. The current renderer still needs shared presentation scheduling; metadata alignment alone is not physical AV synchronization.

native_behavior: Core observes timing under exact current ingress authority and route/scene/consumer guards; the returned liveness predicates are weak metadata. Clocked RTP attaches its snapshot under the same original packet admission. No separate media packet, readiness or idle reader is introduced.

One bounded Connection clock group normalizes its common CNAME/NTP offset once. Each stream/SSRC incarnation has a distinct source identity and current report/route predicates. Waiting, conflicting, zero or unavailable timing remains explicit.

Owned packetizers report current send time with the corresponding destination RTP sample value, after actual successful RTP submissions. All destination streams share one CNAME/clock domain. Reports never count as RTP or establish flow; no detached report timer exists.

A clock incarnation/support/anchor-availability transition retires its prior egress SSRC. Lost mappings cannot reuse a receiver's old clock. Current packet permission, original admission age and bounded queues remain independent of timing metadata.
actual_network_witness: One EdDSA signed local canonical-driver method runs QUIC and WT: accept an authorized sender report before actual PCMU, count no RTP/readiness or queued packet from that report, preserve a deliberate100ms capture phase through actual checked ingress/guarded forwarding/egress, compare its normalized sample mapping with measured before-send/after-admission timestamps within one8kHz sample, then refuse a report after current authorization denial with no media output or idle lease.
